title: Reusable core session authentication seam
description: Objective: expose one reusable, fail-closed core decision for session, credential, proof-of-possession, replay, expiry, and transport authentication, then have authenticateCommand compose it before command capability admission. This is the prerequisite that lets daemon coordination authenticate a session without fabricating a RuntimeCommandEnvelope or forking core precedence. NOT in scope: choosing a cryptographic proof algorithm, persistence, daemon wiring, recipient/effect registries, or coordination mailbox behavior. Owned paths: packages/core/src/identity/authenticate-session.ts, packages/core/src/identity/authenticate-session.js, packages/core/src/identity/authenticate-session.test.ts, packages/core/src/identity/authenticate-command.ts, packages/core/src/index.ts. Production consumer: Durable daemon session and coordination-recipient authority, then task-4afcb06422ed4adb89430b7ea9758d7f. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/core typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/core test && pnpm typecheck.
definitionOfDone: A frozen reusable session-authentication result validates the committed principal, session, credential, presented proof, verifier result, replay result, expiry, generation, client key, and transport facts without accepting caller-supplied positive booleans as authority.

Every refusal preserves the exact stable core code and refusing layer with AUTHENTICATION_FAILED before SESSION_REPLAYED before SESSION_EXPIRED, returns zero principal/session authority, and UNKNOWN or malformed verifier/replay evidence denies.

authenticateCommand delegates session authentication to the new production seam and only then applies its existing exact RuntimeCommand capability check; its public behavior and existing tests remain byte-for-byte compatible.

Focused tests cover success and every refusal/precedence branch, assert code plus layer and zero-authority output, assert generated-case counts, and mutation-drill each production guard so bypassing it turns the focused test red.
The exact verification command exits 0 and the daemon authority prerequisite is named as the real consumer; no proof algorithm, persistence, or coordination capability mapping is introduced here.
taskRails: Keep the core decision pure and dependency-free; injected proof/replay observations are evidence inputs, never inferred truth.
Do not add coordination endpoint strings to RuntimeCommandKind or synthesize fake runtime commands.
Preserve all existing identity authentication reason codes, layers, and precedence.

implementationPlan.description: Measure and pin the baseline before editing. Run `pnpm --filter @moe/core test` and record file/test counts (measured 2026-08-09: 16 files / 239 tests passing). Read packages/core/src/identity/authenticate-command.ts end to end and write down its EXACT current refusal order, which is the contract this task must preserve byte-for-byte: (1) bindingsHold false -> AUTHENTICATION_FAILED; (2) verifyProof throws OR returns !== true -> AUTHENTICATION_FAILED; (3) checkReplay throws OR returns a value that is neither "FRESH" nor "REPLAYED" -> AUTHENTICATION_FAILED; (4) replay === "REPLAYED" OR !isCurrentGeneration(session, credential) -> SESSION_REPLAYED; (5) session.status !== "ACTIVE" -> SESSION_REPLAYED; (6) !isSessionUsableAt(session, now) -> SESSION_EXPIRED; (7) !session.transportIds.includes(transportId) -> CAPABILITY_DENIED; (8) capability match / step-up window -> CAPABILITY_DENIED. Guards 1-7 move to the new seam. Guard 8 (matchCapability + STEP_UP_WINDOW) STAYS in authenticateCommand and is not touched. Do not start editing until this list is written down; it is the acceptance oracle for every later step.
implementationPlan.note: Fresh baseline: `pnpm --filter @moe/core test` exit 0; 16 files / 239 tests passed. `authenticate-command.ts` is 196 physical lines and `authenticate-command.test.ts` is 232. Read the production module end to end and confirmed the exact 8-stage refusal order, with guards 1-7 assigned to the new seam and capability/step-up remaining command-only.

implementationPlan.description: Implement packages/core/src/identity/authenticate-session.ts to turn the tests green. Export: SESSION_AUTH_LAYERS = Object.freeze(["BINDING","PROOF","REPLAY","GENERATION","SESSION_STATE","EXPIRY","TRANSPORT"] as const); type SessionAuthLayer; type SessionAuthCode = "AUTHENTICATION_FAILED" | "SESSION_REPLAYED" | "SESSION_EXPIRED" | "CAPABILITY_DENIED"; interface AuthenticatedSessionFacts { principalId, principalKind, profileRevisionId, sessionId, clientKeyId, projectId, transportId }; SessionAuthenticationResult = { ok: true; facts: AuthenticatedSessionFacts } | { ok: false; code: SessionAuthCode; layer: SessionAuthLayer } — the refusal arm carries NO facts field at all, so zero authority is a type-level guarantee, not a convention. MOVE PresentedProof, ProofChallenge and ReplayOutcome here verbatim from authenticate-command.ts (they are envelope-independent). Input is SessionAuthenticationInput: principal, session, credential, projectId, transportId, now, requestId, requestDigest, presentedCredentialId, proof, verifyProof, checkReplay. requestId/requestDigest/presentedCredentialId are the three scalars authenticateCommand currently reads off the envelope (commandId, requestDigest, sessionCredential) — this is exactly how a non-command caller authenticates without fabricating a RuntimeCommandEnvelope (task rail 2). Port bindingsHold unchanged except that the three envelope reads become those scalars, and add isNonEmpty checks on requestId/requestDigest/presentedCredentialId since there is no envelope decoder upstream to have validated them. Rebuild the ProofChallenge from records only ({ commandId: requestId, requestDigest, credentialId: credential.credentialId, clientKeyId: session.clientKeyId }) and never read input.proof past bindingsHold, preserving the existing defence against a caller-attached verified flag. Wrap verifyProof and checkReplay in try/catch; a throw or any non-"FRESH"/"REPLAYED" value denies (UNKNOWN never authorizes, epic rail 4). Import only from ./identity-session.js — no @moe/contracts, no createRuntimeError; the seam returns a code string and the caller maps it (task rail 1: pure and dependency-free). Freeze both result arms. Also create the bridge packages/core/src/identity/authenticate-session.js containing EXACTLY the bytes `export * from "./authenticate-session.ts";` plus a single LF — runtime-entrypoint.test.ts compares bridge bytes through utf8 and a CRLF ending fails there while git diff --stat shows nothing. Target under 250 lines.

Compose the seam into authenticateCommand without changing its public behavior. In packages/core/src/identity/authenticate-command.ts: delete the local bindingsHold, isNonEmpty and STEP_UP-unrelated guards 1-7, and re-export the moved types with `export type { PresentedProof, ProofChallenge, ReplayOutcome } from "./authenticate-session.js";` so identity/index.ts's existing export block keeps resolving those three names unchanged. authenticateCommand now computes correlationId as today, calls authenticateSession({ ...records, requestId: envelope.commandId, requestDigest: envelope.requestDigest, presentedCredentialId: envelope.sessionCredential, ... }) — guarding the envelope read itself so a null/non-object envelope still yields AUTHENTICATION_FAILED with correlationId "" exactly as now — and on !ok returns deny(result.code, correlationId), discarding the layer. The layer is deliberately NOT surfaced through authenticateCommand: RuntimeError has no layer field and adding one would change its public shape, which DoD item 3 forbids. Then apply the UNCHANGED capability block: matchCapability, then requiresRecentStepUp against STEP_UP_WINDOW, then the same frozen AuthorizationContext. AuthenticateCommandInput, AuthenticateCommandResult and AuthorizationContext keep their exact field sets. Publish the new seam by ADDING to packages/core/src/identity/index.ts: `export { authenticateSession, SESSION_AUTH_LAYERS } from "./authenticate-session.js";` and a type block for AuthenticatedSessionFacts, SessionAuthCode, SessionAuthLayer, SessionAuthenticationInput, SessionAuthenticationResult. Do NOT edit packages/core/src/index.ts — it already does `export * from "./identity/index.js"` and its own comment records the decision that identity is published through the curated area seam rather than per-module blocks; adding a block there would create the second sync point that comment exists to prevent. Run `pnpm --filter @moe/core test` — authenticate-command.test.ts must pass with ZERO edits to that file. If it needs an edit, the refactor changed behavior: revert and fix the seam, do not adjust the test.

Regression sweep. Run `pnpm --filter @moe/core typecheck` then `pnpm --filter @moe/core test` and compare against the step-1 baseline: all 16 prior files still pass, count rises only by the new authenticate-session.test.ts. planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
COORDINATION WITH task-8470a86013c94f08be640b568c2671da — ANSWERED BY MEASUREMENT: THE TWO SEAMS ARE GENUINELY SEPARATE AND MUST NOT BE MERGED.

The governor asked whether this task's seam is where the daemon HTTP Authenticator's policy belongs. It is not, and the reason is structural rather than stylistic. apps/daemon/src/http/http-contract.ts:110 declares `authenticate(credential: string | null)`. http-adapter.ts calls it at line 154; decodeRuntimeCommandEnvelopeBytes runs at line 163. The documented pipeline at http-adapter.ts:33 is `authenticate -> compatibility -> bounded decode -> registry -> authorize`, and the contract comment states the ordering exists so attacker bytes are never decoded for an unauthenticated caller. A PRE-DECODE gate cannot supply commandId, requestDigest or a proof-of-possession — those only exist after decoding. authenticateSession requires all three. So the HTTP port is a cheap transport-credential gate that necessarily runs BEFORE the facts this seam consumes exist. Collapsing them would force decoding untrusted bytes before authentication, which is the exact inversion the daemon boundary was built to prevent. task-8470a860 is therefore NOT named as a consumer, and nobody should later merge these two on the grounds that both are 'authentication'. They compose in sequence; they are not the same decision.

CONSUMER EDGE (Clause 1, option a — named consumer task): task-21713cf152c047c597da9765d8d95510 'Durable daemon session authority'. Verified on disk in .moe/tasks/: its description states 'Depends on task-b4f12e63baca4ecc9f2c159ed3c3ad78' and it owns apps/daemon/src/identity/session-authority*.ts, which is where the SqliteEventStore-backed records, the concrete proof verifier and the durable replay guard land — i.e. the real implementations of the verifyProof/checkReplay evidence inputs this seam declares. Downstream: task-04e4367443214a588ed6277b92969a33, then task-4afcb06422ed4adb89430b7ea9758d7f.

SCALAR TRIPLE OVER ENVELOPE ABSTRACTION. Rejected: passing a structural subset type of RuntimeCommandEnvelope. It keeps command vocabulary in a decision that must serve non-command transports and invites a caller to synthesize a partial envelope, which task rail 2 forbids. Chosen: the seam takes requestId, requestDigest and presentedCredentialId as plain scalars; authenticateCommand supplies envelope.commandId, envelope.requestDigest and envelope.sessionCredential. ProofChallenge keeps its exact existing field names (commandId/requestDigest/credentialId/clientKeyId) so the exported type and the verifier contract are unchanged.

CODE STRING OVER RuntimeError. Rejected: returning a RuntimeError from the seam. It would import @moe/contracts into a decision task rail 1 requires to be pure, and would force a correlationId the seam has no business knowing. Chosen: the seam returns {code, layer}; authenticateCommand maps code through its existing deny() helper, so the RuntimeError produced is byte-identical to today's.

TYPE-LEVEL ZERO AUTHORITY. Rejected: a result type carrying an always-null facts field on refusal. Chosen: the refusal arm has no facts key at all, so 'returns zero principal/session authority' is enforced by the compiler and provable by an exact Object.keys assertion rather than by a lookup that happens to return null.

planningNotes.risks:
1. BYTE-FOR-BYTE COMPATIBILITY IS THE HARDEST CONSTRAINT. authenticate-command.test.ts (232 lines) already pins the combined-fault precedence cases: AUTHENTICATION_FAILED over replay and expiry, SESSION_REPLAYED over SESSION_EXPIRED, SESSION_EXPIRED over CAPABILITY_DENIED. If that file needs even one edit to stay green, behavior changed — revert the seam, do not adjust the test.

2. THE ENVELOPE READ IS ITSELF A GUARD. Today `input.envelope?.correlationId ?? ""` plus bindingsHold means a null or non-object envelope denies with AUTHENTICATION_FAILED and an empty correlationId. Reading envelope.commandId eagerly to build the seam input would throw instead of denying. Guard the envelope read in authenticateCommand before calling the seam.

3. BINDINGS THE ENVELOPE USED TO GUARANTEE. Inside authenticateCommand the envelope had already been decoded, so commandId and requestDigest were structurally valid. A coordination caller has no decoder upstream. The seam must isNonEmpty-check requestId, requestDigest and presentedCredentialId itself or it is weaker than the code it replaces.

4. TRANSPORT REFUSAL RETURNS CAPABILITY_DENIED, NOT A SESSION CODE. Guard 7 moves into the seam but keeps the CAPABILITY_DENIED code. It looks like a capability check and is not one; do not 'correct' it to SESSION_EXPIRED or leave it behind in authenticateCommand — either change breaks a pinned precedence test.

5. CRLF BRIDGE. Covered in step 3, repeated because it is the failure that hides from git diff --stat: write authenticate-session.js with LF only.

6. SHARED WORKING DIRECTORY. Every agent works in D:/projexts/moe-next. During the mutation drills another task's completion hook can commit a tree containing your live drill edit, leaving git status clean while the mutation is still in the file. Trust the red test; verify restoration with `git diff -- <path>` returning empty, not with status. Equally, if the repo-wide `pnpm typecheck` leg is red, attribute failures by path before treating them as this task's defect.

7. MUTATION DRILLS ARE THE ONLY PROOF THE TESTS ARE LIVE. Nine refusal cases that all assert 'not ok' would pass against a seam that denies everything unconditionally. The layer assertion plus the swap-one-layer drill is what makes the suite non-vacuous.

8. LINE BUDGET. authenticate-command.ts drops to roughly 110 lines after extraction and authenticate-session.ts should land near 200. Both are under the 250 target; if the seam approaches 250, split the record-binding helpers rather than trimming comments. The cap is per file, not per task.
